caption: The video captures a narrow forest stream from a fixed vantage point, its calm foreground water mirroring the bright sky and the green canopy lining both banks. A single grey rock breaks the surface left of center, a fallen log rests on the right bank, and two lens-flare artifacts—a pale green disc and a reddish-orange streak—stay fixed. The water surface is never still: fine ripples and shimmer travel across the foreground, warping the reflected trees and sky so their mirrored images break apart and re-form. Small pale flecks on the left side of the pool drift and redistribute their pattern over time. Farther upstream, where the channel narrows, faster-flowing water keeps moving steadily with an ongoing current. The trees, rock, log, and flares stay fixed, confirming the camera neither translates nor zooms. The rippling and flow are already underway when the view opens and continue without pause as it closes.
